comment: Discovery profile (ck.profile.discovery.v1) black-box vectors covering: (a) advertise vs core/extension tier filtering — `core` surfaces are implied by claiming v1 protocol support, `extension` surfaces require explicit advertisement; (b) `interop_bridge` tier handling when an external protocol (MIMI / Applet) is supported vs NOT supported — bridge operations are NEVER implied and are not part of any core/extension profile; (c) post-C16 (spec 2026-05-08) surface naming: `blob_storage` (split out from a previous combined media surface), `realtime_media` (renamed from media), `moderation_reports` (renamed from moderation). The validator walks each vector, checks the advertised `surfaces[]` against the core/extension/interop_bridge tier rules, and asserts the SUT capability response matches the spec-mandated discovery semantics.

tier_rules.core: MUST be advertised whenever the SUT claims `ck.profile.cokret_v1.core`. Absent advertisement is a discovery contract violation; the discovery client MUST treat the SUT as non-conformant.
tier_rules.extension: MUST be advertised explicitly. A core-only SUT MUST NOT auto-imply any extension surface. Discovery clients MUST gate extension calls on the surface appearing in the advertised set.
tier_rules.interop_bridge: Bridge surfaces MUST be advertised only when the external protocol (MIMI Internet-Drafts / third-party Applet host) is actually supported. Bridge advertisement implies neither core nor extension support. Discovery clients MUST NOT assume an interop_bridge surface implies the corresponding `bridges_to` in-spec surface is supported (and vice-versa).
tier_rules.deployment_local: Deployment-specific surfaces (account_auth, etc) — out of scope for discovery profile vectors.

surface_catalog.comment: Spec authority: registry/operation-registry.json `surface_groups[]`. Each entry pairs a canonical surface name with its tier; the validator uses this to detect drift between the fixture and the live operation registry.

expected.comment_c16: Post-C16 (spec 2026-05-08) blob_storage was split out as its own surface from a previous combined media-like surface. A SUT advertising blob_storage gets blob ops only — NOT realtime_media, NOT moderation_reports.
realtime_media (the WebRTC ICE config surface) does NOT imply blob_storage; the spec split is enforced at discovery.
moderation_reports is the post-C16 canonical surface name. Pre-C16 fixtures used `moderation`; this is now drift and would fail validator surface-name lookup.

expected.comment: interop_bridge tier surfaces MUST be explicitly advertised, and only when the external protocol is actually supported. Advertising mimi_interop does NOT imply applet or any extension surface.

Discovery client tries to invoke a MIMI bridge op against an SUT that did NOT advertise mimi_interop and does NOT support MIMI. The SUT MUST reject (or 404) and the discovery client MUST gate the call on the advertised set, not on naive heuristics.
Calling an extension op (blob.upload) on a core-only SUT MUST be rejected. Extension surfaces are NEVER implied by core.

Even though mimi_interop's bridge ops have a `bridges_to` link to in-spec ops (e.g. ck.mimi.submit_message bridges_to ck.events.submit), advertising mimi_interop is NOT advertising events_sync. The events_sync surface IS advertised here so the call would actually succeed — the negative is the reverse direction: a discovery client must NOT advertise mimi_interop and assume that gives it events_sync access. The SUT here did advertise events_sync, so this vector is structural: the client must call ops via the actual advertised surface, not via a bridge implication.
